blocks.text: A Māori GIS Conference was held in Christchurch on 13–15 May 2009. Massey University's research record identifies a presentation that May titled Towards developing and applying an Iwi/Hapū based GIS system, with Jonathan Procter, Garth Harmsworth and collaborators among its authors. This is direct evidence of a practitioner forum and a specific technical contribution. Contemporary documents are still needed to settle the conference's complete organising committee and programme.

blocks.text: A further Māori GIS conference took place in Lower Hutt in October 2010. Archaeologist Simon Bickler's CV records his presentation on the New Zealand Archaeological Association's ArchSite GIS database, and a University of Otago planning document independently records student attendance at a Wellington-region Māori GIS conference in 2010. Te Kāhui Manu Hōkai subsequently developed as an association for Māori GIS practitioners. Its incorporated society was registered on 14 June 2013 and dissolved on 11 June 2018, according to the New Zealand Companies Office register (society number 2582124; NZBN 9429043247875). The association's name remained in use for the PLACE19 conference in 2019 and was associated with LINZ and GIS Journey Limited's Ngā Poutama Matawhenua mapping wānanga from October 2020. These later activities should not be taken as evidence that the dissolved incorporated society continued as a registered legal entity.
